title: Verbosity-Reward Echo: Do Models Pad Confident Prose When Honesty Requires Brevity?

original_idea.body: Verbosity-Reward Echo. Problem: whether small open chat models show a correlation between answer length and overconfidence (length as a tell for fabrication) is a concrete testable pattern. Direction: on a factual QA set, measure answer length, expressed confidence, and correctness per item, test whether longer answers are systematically more confident-yet-wrong, characterize the length-vs-honesty relationship per model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (length-as-fabrication-proxy -> free monitor heuristic) but catastrophic-risk link is a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Measure length/confidence/correctness on labeled QA; correlation analysis.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped correlation study with clear metrics.

novelty.reasoning: Verbosity bias noted; length-as-fabrication-tell correlation may be a fresh angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Verbosity bias is noted; the length-predicts-overconfidence correlation as a heuristic is plausibly open.
